free_tier.stated: The free Basic tier is 5 GB of Data Store storage, 200 compute units per year and 1 concurrent job, where the page states "1 Compute Unit equals 1 Core Hour on a CPU". Paid individual tiers are Regular at USD 200 per year for 50 GB, 1,000 compute units and 2 concurrent jobs, and Pro at USD 400 per year for 4 TB, 25,000 compute units and 4 concurrent jobs, with GPU access by request on the two paid tiers only.

record.interface_detail: Data Store: WebDAV, SFTP, iCommands and GoCommands command-line tools, and the Discovery Environment web console; Terrain REST API, where the subscription page lists Advanced Features & APIs for Pro and Commercial only
record.tooling: GoCommands and iCommands command-line tools for the Data Store, and the Terrain REST API; Discovery Environment web console
record.chaining: CyVerse is the funding parent of the Galaxy Main hardware allocation, so the two accounts sit on overlapping machines; the useful composition is the paid Pro tier, where USD 400 a year buys 25,000 core-hours and 4 TB on the same infrastructure that hosts Galaxy, which is a batch analysis machine with a shell rather than Galaxy wrappers.

limits.value: 5 GB of storage and 200 core-hours a year on the free tier, enforced since 1 March 2025, and the user portal states that data above quota is deleted and is not recoverable.

record.notes: The free tier is small enough that recording it as capacity would mislead: 200 core-hours a year is one afternoon of a single core. Its value is the paid tier as a price floor, and the enforcement history as a reliability fact. It is not the cheapest cost per core-hour in the file: the DesignSafe record carries a TACC purchase rate near USD 0.008 to USD 0.01 per core-hour, but that is a quote-based purchase from a national laboratory rather than a published annual plan. CyVerse also removes accounts for inactivity, announced on its own 404 page, which is a fact a reader storing data there needs.

free_tier.stated: 5 GB default for every account, explicitly for 'all domestic and international CyVerse account holders'. Above that it is paid: $125/TB/year single-copy up to 4 TB, $105/TB/year beyond, and $250/TB/year for 2025 double-copy. Community Data folders can be granted larger allocations on application, and published data in the Data Commons can be larger. But the free self-serve number is 5 GB.

retention.stated: US NSF-funded, data mirrored at Arizona and TACC. Explicitly not an archive: 'The Data Store is not intended for permanent, archival storage.'

egress.terms: Free. IRODS-backed, anonymous public links for published data; the Data Commons is browsable without an account.

record.tooling: iRODS with iCommands, plus a REST API and the Discovery Environment UI. Mature and scriptable, but the data model is iRODS rather than S3/WebDAV, so rclone needs the iRODS plugin rather than a stock backend.
record.chaining: 5 GB per account is trivially repeatable in principle, but each account needs its own email and the allocation is tied to identity, so it does not compose into anything large without deliberate account farming. Community Data folders are the only legitimate multiplier and they are reviewed.

limits.value: Application, and published data in the Data Commons can be larger. But the free self-serve.

record.limits_note: Free tier allocation is limited, and paid storage costs $125 per TB per year (approximately $10.40 per TB per month). Community Released Data folders require a current paid subscription.
